institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Languague was important, I choose a destination with high english speaking skills. I also chose a destination with good career opportunuties and high education level. Lastly, I chose a destination with a very different culture, climate and history compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, there was a thorough onboarding from HKUST, so this part was good. There was some confusion between a lot of apps and sites, but not anymore than you would find at any other university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Welcoming days to onboard new exchange students. This was several days, and otherwise there was a number and email to contact if you needed further assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The only option was a 2 man shared dormitory room, with somewhat random bathroom accomodation. I did not choose which hall to live in, but there was an option to find a new roommate, if you were not satisfied with the one appointed to you. There was the option to choose whether to live in a compus hall, or their single off-campus hall.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: As far as I know, there was none except a private mini-fridge, a common large fridge, a common microwave and a common cutting board with knives. I don't think there were any available meal plans, but there were cafeterias, restaurants and fastfood options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are shared bathrooms and no real cooking facilities, and you share a small room with a roommate, but on the other hand it would be very expensive to find better housing solutions in Hong Kong.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was a visa application that the host university handled, then there was a lot of personal information that you had to provide to the university personally. Upon arrival, the real course registration period started. The course registration was the worst part of the process. It could have been much more clear and done much earlier before the semester start.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a phone number and email to contact. I could not find a physical office for guidance, when I needed help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a difficult process, because there was a pre-registration, but at that point I didn't know if the courses were valid or not, if I had the requirements to take that course, and if it was even a course in the spring or autumn semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to plan your courses as precisely as possible beforehand, and research if it's held during your exchange stay, and research whether you need aan approval if you don't have prerequisite courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There was a mixed level, because I had courses meant for first, second, third and fourth year students. I also had courses from different subjects, so it was very mixed, but the level of education was generally very high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's less free, since many courses have mandatory participation. It was also a bit less interactive with professors and TAs, but this depends heavily on the specific course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
VBA programming bridging course
Programming with C++
Cryptography
International Trade and Investment
Tech startup and entrepreneurs ecosystem: growth and innovation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Tech startup and entrepreneurs ecosystem: growth and innovation, because this course had a lot of international students, and the entire atmosphere was international by nature. The professor was very interactive with students, and spoke english well. The course put high emphasis on participation, but was not stressful, since there waas not a high workload in terms of assignments and midterms. The final exam was a group presentation.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The campus is some distance from the inner city, so you take unexpectedly many ubers and taxis, especially if you need to get home late at night.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I did not need to buy any books, so that was cheap. Generally, I was not surprised by anything being too expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are societies for a lot of different hobbies. Most of them are officially sponsored by the school, and there are also some, which are still just completely student-run. There are about 20 sport societes, but since the football team was only for full- students, I joined many unofficial football groups.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join football groups where you play university staff, or the one where you play the smaller fields.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: My favourite activites were hiking, sailing, Happy Valley horse racing and the nightlife of Hong Kong. When you have several days free, I recommend you travel to Shenzhen, Macau and Guanzhou, and these are just the nearby easy options.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough, but the biggest difference was living on-campus, compared to living privately in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My best tips for socializing is go out at night in the first weeks, and specifically go to Mr. Wongs and Happy Valley races, where international sutdents from all universites in Hong Kong socialize. Other tips would be to try sports societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find the cuture hard to adapt to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hong Kong is very safe, and you will not find many people looking for trouble, if any.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Socialize a lot early.

Explore Hong Kong and perhaps also mainland China or Macau. HKUST campus can be like living in a bubble.

Carefully plan your courses. Don't make it hard for yourself. I wish I took easier, less technical courses, so I could have enjoyed more time to learn about Hong Kong and travelling.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to find experiences outside of campus, whether in nature or in the city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a totally different part of the world. I learned about a new culture and met new friends, both Hong Kong locals and international students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I wish I put more emphasis on socializing in the beginning. You meet so many people, but I wish I focused on getting a close friend group early. This took some more time for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
